extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, ORR-contracted care provider facilities, DHS referring agencies, child-welfare advocates, and public commenters on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_short: ORR placement criteria for unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory standards and placement criteria that the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) would use to determine where and how to place unaccompanied children in ORR custody, including factors for restrictive placements, timelines, provider obligations, and services for children of unaccompanied children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of referral and assessment information for placement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR documents and reviews the unaccompanied child's biographical and apprehension information, including any information about an unaccompanied child's health status, as submitted by the referring Federal agency, and would be able to utilize information provided by the referring Federal agency, child assessment tools, interviews, and pertinent documentation to determine placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may obtain any relevant records from local, State, and Federal agencies regarding an unaccompanied child to inform placement decisions; this information is 'vital in carrying out ORR's general duty to coordinate the care and placement' and to determine whether a restrictive placement may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review frequency for restrictive placements
rubrics_metrics.description: The placement of an unaccompanied child in a restrictive placement must be reviewed at least every thirty days to determine if such placement remains warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies ORR's existing policy of reviewing all restrictive placements (not only secure placements) at least every thirty days and exceeds TVPRA's requirement for secure placement reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic placement efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must make reasonable efforts to provide placements in those geographical areas where DHS encounters the majority of unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to facilitate orderly and expeditious transfer of children from DHS border facilities to ORR care provider facilities and reflects the FSA paragraph 6; ORR will also consider other placement considerations in §§ 410.1103(a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider facility acceptance and denial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must accept all unaccompanied children placed by ORR except in limited circumstances, and any denial must be a written request to ORR providing individualized reasons and must be approved by ORR before denying placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible reasons to deny placement are limited to: (1) lack of available bed space; (2) conflict with the care provider facility's state or local licensing rules; (3) initial placement involves a child with significant physical or mental illness for which the referring agency does not provide a medical clearance; or (4) for a child with a disability, the facility concludes it cannot meet the child's disability-related needs without fundamentally altering its program even with reasonable modifications and additional ORR support. ORR may follow up with facilities about denials to find solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for identifying appropriate placement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would identify an appropriate placement for the unaccompanied child at a care provider facility within 24 hours of receiving the referring agency's notification, whenever possible, and no later than 48 hours, barring exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influx or emergency situations are exceptions; in such events ORR would place children as expeditiously as possible per subpart I (Emergency and Influx Operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Default placement in a standard (non-restrictive) program
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would place all unaccompanied children in a standard program that is not a restrictive placement after transfer to ORR custody, except where the child meets criteria for restrictive placement or in an emergency/influx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements TVPRA's requirement to place children 'in the least restrictive setting that is in the best interest of the child' and is subject to exceptions enumerated in proposed §§ 410.1104 and 410.1105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consider less restrictive alternatives before secure placement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would not place a child in a secure facility if less restrictive alternative placements are available and appropriate under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining whether a less restrictive placement is available for a child with a disability, ORR must consider reasonable modifications to policies/practices/procedures or provision of auxiliary aids and services consistent with Section 504 (29 U.S.C. 794(a)), but is not required to take actions that would fundamentally alter the nature of the program. Less restrictive alternatives may include heightened supervision facilities or other licensed programs (standard programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated criteria for placement in a secure facility (non-RTC)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may place a child in a secure facility (that is not an RTC) only if the child meets one of three specific criteria: (i) charged with or convicted of a crime or subject of delinquency proceedings where ORR deems the child poses a danger to self or others (excluding isolated or petty offenses); (ii) committed, or made credible threats to commit, a violent or malicious act while in DHS/ORR custody or in the presence of an immigration officer, ORR official, or ORR contracted staff; or (iii) engaged while in a restrictive placement in conduct unacceptably disruptive of normal facility functioning and removal is necessary to ensure welfare of the child or others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR omits 'chargeable' language from prior rules because ORR is not a law enforcement agency; runaway risk is not listed as a permissible reason for secure placement; disruptive conduct examples include substance/alcohol use, stealing, fighting, intimidation, or sexually predatory behavior. ORR prefers stepping up to heightened supervision before secure placement when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for placement in a heightened supervision facility
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may place children in a heightened supervision facility at initial placement or by transfer, and would consider specific factors in determining such placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include: (1) unacceptably disruptive behavior in a shelter such that transfer is necessary to ensure welfare of the child or others; (2) the child is a runaway risk per § 410.1107; (3) a pattern of severity of behavior requiring increased supervision by trained staff; (4) a non-violent criminal or delinquent history not warranting secure facility placement (e.g., isolated or petty offenses); and (5) the child is assessed as ready for step-down from a secure facility, including an RTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: RTC placement clinical and evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child may be placed at an RTC only if it is the least restrictive setting in the child's best interest and appropriate to the child's age and individualized needs, and where serious mental or behavioral health issues exist an RTC placement requires evaluation and determination by a licensed psychologist or psychiatrist that the child is a danger to self or others supported by 'clear and convincing evidence' documented in the case file or referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR would apply the same criteria used for secure facilities to assess danger to self or others in RTC placement. For children with disabilities, ORR must consider whether reasonable modifications or auxiliary aids could reduce danger; ORR is not required to implement changes that fundamentally alter a program. ORR may place children in out-of-network (OON) RTCs when a licensed clinician determines OON care is necessary; OON RTCs are vetted via state licensing and may be reviewed with Federal agencies or P&A systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and placement for children needing particular services or treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would assess unaccompanied children for individualized needs requiring particular services, equipment, and treatment by staff (moving away from the FSA 'special needs' terminology) and place such children, whenever possible, in inclusive licensed programs that provide needed services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination is not limited to children identified as having a disability; an array of individualized needs can trigger this requirement. This section aligns with the Rehabilitation Act's requirement to administer programs in the most integrated setting appropriate to individuals with disabilities. Examples of individualized needs are illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runaway risk (risk of flight) factors for placement decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would consider specific factors when evaluating whether a child is a runaway risk for placement purposes, interpreting 'risk of flight' to include runaway risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified factors include: (a) the child is currently under a final order of removal; (b) immigration history including prior breach of bond, failure to appear, evidence of indebtedness to organized smugglers for transport, or previous removal pursuant to a final order; (c) prior absconding or attempted absconding from state or Federal custody. ORR also proposes considering (d) behaviors indicative of flight or expressed intent to run away, and (e) evidence of indebtedness to, strong trauma bonding with, or threats from a trafficker in persons or drugs. ORR considered but did not codify voluntary departure as a factor based on experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and services for children of unaccompanied children
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes to place unaccompanied children and their children together at the same care provider facilities except in unusual or emergency situations, and to provide children of unaccompanied children the same care and services as ORR provides to unaccompanied children as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual or emergency exceptions include hospitalization or need for specialized care the facility cannot provide, a request by the unaccompanied child for alternate placement of their child, or substantiated allegations of abuse/neglect requiring temporary separation. U.S. citizen children of unaccompanied children are eligible for mainstream public benefits (e.g., Medicaid); care provider facilities shall submit applications for such benefits and should exhaust public benefits to the greatest extent practicable before using ORR-funded services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of best interests of other children and staff safety in placement
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether placement in an RTC or any care provider facility is appropriate, ORR considers the best interests of other unaccompanied children housed at the receiving facility and the safety of care provider facility staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR states it is authorized under the TVPRA to consider the safety and well-being of other children and staff when making placement determinations; this consideration may affect whether a particular placement is appropriate even if it meets an individual child's clinical criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and scope clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes updated terminology and scope rules, such as replacing 'escape risk' with 'runaway risk' and avoiding reliance on FSA provisions tied to detention following apprehension (which ORR does not perform).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR also elects not to codify certain FSA exceptions that pertain to DHS detention or 'chargeable' delinquency determinations because ORR is not a law enforcement agency; instead ORR adapts the standards to its statutory role and operational experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider vetting and oversight for out-of-network RTCs
rubrics_metrics.description: OON RTCs used for placement must be vetted prior to placement via state licensing authorities to ensure the program is in good standing and complying with applicable state and local welfare laws, building, fire, health, and safety codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may confer with other Federal agencies and protection and advocacy (P&A) systems during vetting to determine appropriateness; a child placed at an OON RTC remains in ORR legal custody and ORR will monitor progress and required services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation standard for clinical RTC determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: An RTC placement for serious mental or behavioral health issues requires documentation of a determination by a licensed psychologist or psychiatrist that an RTC is appropriate, supported by clear and convincing evidence in the child's case file or referral documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation requirement is consistent with the Secretary of HHS factors under the TVPRA and mirrors provisions of the 2019 Final Rule; licensed clinician consultation is required for such high-level placements.
